source: Grierson, Linguistic Survey of India, Volume IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages (1906), Tūri section
edition: Original 1906 Calcutta printing, not a later reprint
rights: Public domain original (1906); Wikimedia Commons public-domain scan. Only two public-domain printed page images and factual transcriptions are packaged; the 701-page DjVu is a local cache.
scope: Complete Turi chapter, printed pp.128–134 (DjVu147–153):24 prose units,117 Ranchi,102 Jashpur and109 Sarangarh aligned units; free translations and footnotes reviewed.
excluded_scope: Three prose comparison/conjecture controls and one bracketed editorial insertion are contextual only.
Unattributed introductory implement names and isolated morphological endings are accounted for in prose-context-dispositions.json, not independently assigned to Turi.
Other LSI IV languages are outside this chapter.
method: Visually read source pages; Tesseract English OCR retained as a comparison hint, never authoritative for form diacritics. Every selected item manually checked against the printed page.
coordinates: All four historical sites retain blank coordinates; unspecified prose is not assigned a dialect.
etymology: No graph edges. Grierson's Santali comparison and conjectural reinterpretation of hor are editorial claims, not independently established links.
overlap: 57 exact site/form/gloss reuses within chapter preserve all source locators. Cross-source compiled verification deferred under no-build instruction.
